data.cultural_impact: During Ramadan, Muslims around the world dedicate the month of Siyam to practicing self-discipline and devotion by fasting from dawn till sunset, refraining from worldly desires, focusing on prayer and remembrance of Allah, and practicing kindness and generosity towards others.
data.spiritual_significance: Through the practice of fasting during Siyam, Muslims seek to cleanse their souls of impurities, deepen their spiritual connection with Allah, develop self-control and empathy for the less fortunate, and strive towards attaining inner peace and enlightenment. It is a time for introspection and learning self-restraint, encouraging humility, patience, and self-done good deeds.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Siyam is an Arabic term which refers to the practice of fasting during the Islamic month of Ramadan. This practice is based on the teachings of the Quran and the example of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The word Siyam comes from the Arabic root 'saum' which means abstinence or restraint.
historical_references.time_period: Ramadan, Islamic calendar (approximately April-May or May-June in the Gregorian calendar)

historical_references.reference: Siyam was also practiced by early Muslims in pre-Islamic Arabia as a form of penance and self-discipline. It was believed that by fasting during certain months, individuals could seek forgiveness for their sins and draw closer to God. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have practiced Siyam before the revelation of the Quranic verses concerning the obligatory fasting during Ramadan.
